The Impact of Digital Transformation (DX) Adoption on Innovation Performance in SMEs : Focusing on the Moderating Effect of Government Support Programs

Jeon Young Joon

School of Convergence Science Major of Science and Technology Innovation The Graduate School Pusan National University

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content:
With the acceleration of digitalization across various industries and daily  life, the

way  of   life   is  changing,  and  convenience  in  daily  living   is  increasing.  This

phenomenon  is  referred to as  Digital Transformation  (DX).  Digital transformation

applies digital technologies across society, transforming the existing social structure,

and innovating  traditional operations and services using new  digital technologies.

The chain from production, manufacturing, distribution, to consumption has evolved

at a faster pace due to the continuous development of digital technologies. Digital

transformation has become a crucial factor in enhancing business performance by

innovating business models, operational processes, and customer experiences using

digital  technologies such  as  big  data,  artificial  intelligence  (AI),  the  Internet  of

Things (IoT), cloud computing, robotics, and 3D printing.

According  to  statistics from  the  Ministry  of SMEs and  Startups  in  2022,  the

number of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Korea was 7.28  million,

accounting for 99.9% of  all businesses. Despite the significant share SMEs hold in

the  national  economy,  they   still  face  various  challenges  in  adopting  digital

transformation and  other  innovation  activities due  to  constraints  in human and

material resources.  In response to these resource  limitations, various government

support programs have been implemented. However, government support remains

insufficient, and issues such as the gap and imbalance between large corporations

and SMEs  are   still  prominent.  Therefore,  continuous  policy  support  from  the

government  is necessary to complement these limitations, facilitate the adoption of

digital  transformation, and  help SMEs  explore  niche  markets and develop new

products, areas where large corporations tend not to invest.

This  study   empirically  analyzes  the  impact  of  the  adoption  of   digital

transformation  on  innovation  performance,  such  as  product  innovation  and

business   process   innovation,   in  SMEs.   Furthermore,    it  examines  whether

government  support  programs  (tax  incentives,  financial  support,  technological

support,  and  workforce  support)  moderate  the  relationship  between   digital

transformation adoption and innovation performance. To  this end, data from the

2022 Korean Innovation Survey (KIS) in the manufacturing sector, conducted by the

Science and Technology Policy Institute (STEPI), was used for the analysis. For this

study, 3,281 companies excluding mid-sized and  large  enterprises were  selected

from a sample  of  4,000  original  data  points  to  analyze  the impact  of  digital

transformation adoption on innovation performance in SMEs.

The  results  indicate  that  among  the  digital  technologies  used  in  digital

transformation adoption, big data, cloud computing, robotics, and 3D printing had

a  significant  positive  impact on both  product  innovation and  business  process

innovation in SMEs. Secondly, the study found that financial support programs had

a  significant moderating  effect  in the  relationship between robotics and product

innovation, as  well as between robotics and business process innovation.  Finally,

the  technological  support  program  was  found  to  have  a  significant  positive

moderating  effect  in  the  relationship  between  cloud  computing  and  business

process innovation.

This study  is significant in that  it provides a detailed analysis of the relationship

between  digital transformation adoption and innovation performance, considering

the nine digital technologies and two types of innovation performance as defined

in the Korean Innovation Survey. The findings can be used as a basis for further

research in this area. Additionally,  it can contribute to innovation activities in SMEs,

such as decision-making regarding technology prioritization and the use of current

government support programs  in the process  of adopting  digital  transformation.

For example, SMEs can  first adopt technologies  that have a  significant  positive

impact on innovation performance, such as big  data, cloud computing,  robotics,

and 3D printing, to expect greater innovation outcomes. On the other hand, new

government policies to promote  digital transformation are also necessary. Despite

utilizing  the  government  support  programs  that  are  considered  necessary  to

promote digital transformation, many cases did not show a moderating effect on

the   relationship  between   digital   transformation   adoption  and   innovation

performance.  This  suggests  that  there   is  a  lack  of  information  available  to

companies  regarding  digital  transformation  adoption.  Therefore,  to  increase  the

likelihood of creating innovation outcomes through digital transformation adoption,

the government needs to strengthen  its support  policies  for SMEs. Rather than

merely  continuing  current  policies,  it  is  crucial  to re-examine and segment  the

support programs needed based on the specific digital transformation technologies

being adopted, in order to lower the barriers to digital transformation adoption for

SMEs and ensure efficient implementation.

Keywords:   Digital   Transformation,  Government   Support   Programs,  SMEs,

Moderating   Effects,  Product  Innovation,  Business  Process  Innovation,  Korean

Innovation Survey
